title: Titanium Acetabular Cup
alloyReason: Ti-6Al-4V ELI (Extra Low Interstitials, ASTM F136 / ISO 5832-3) is the medical-grade standard for permanent implantable devices. Its lower oxygen (<0.13%) and iron (<0.25%) content provides superior fracture toughness and fatigue resistance compared to standard Grade 5, making it mandatory for orthopedic and spinal implants.
commonFailures: Surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (ASTM F86)
Thread damage from improper installation torque exceeding recommended values
Galvanic corrosion at interface with dissimilar metals in electrolyte environments

faq.q: What is a titanium acetabular cup?
faq.a: A titanium acetabular cup is a precision-machined orthopedic joints component used in porous biomimetic acetabular cup (ebm 3d-printed). Manufactured from Ti-6Al-4V ELI (ASTM F136) for optimal strength, corrosion resistance, and weight savings.

faq.q: What is the typical application for titanium acetabular cup?
faq.a: Titanium Acetabular Cup is designed for porous biomimetic acetabular cup (ebm 3d-printed). The Ti-6Al-4V ELI (ASTM F136) grade is selected to provide the optimal balance of strength, fatigue life, and environmental resistance for this specific application.

faq.q: How is titanium acetabular cup manufactured?
faq.a: Titanium Acetabular Cup is manufactured using VAR melting. Critical process controls include tool path optimization, coolant temperature management, and dimensional verification at each operation.

faq.q: What is the most common issue with titanium acetabular cup?
faq.a: The most common issue is surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (astm f86). Mitigation includes proper process control, material certification, and adherence to recommended installation procedures and torque values.
